issue.title: Notification-gate word/agent schemas still allow any non-whitespace
issue.description:
## Bug

- **Location:** `src/sase/notification_gates/model_inputs.py` (`_TYPE_SCHEMA_FRAGMENTS` for `InputType.WORD` and `InputType.AGENT`)

Notification-gate form schemas still compile `word` and `agent` fields to `^\S+` (any non-whitespace), while `InputArg.validate_and_convert` now enforces `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (plus an optional leading `@` for `agent`). The module comment requires the two layers to agree; they no longer do after sase-1sb.4 (`22e1ef1249`).

A gate option whose command consumes a `word` input therefore accepts values such as `owner/repo` or `foo:bar` at schema validation, then the command layer rejects them. Non-Python clients that honor the compiled JSON Schema inherit the looser pattern.

This is the same incomplete-audit gap as plan:202611/fix_gh_owner_repo_refs.md (the `#gh` macro kept `word` after the charset narrowing). Align the compiled `pattern` with `_WORD_RE` / `_AGENT_RE` in `src/sase/macro/models.py`, keep the `(?![\s\S])` end-of-input anchor, and update `docs/reference/automation/notification-gates.md` if its `word` row still says "no whitespace". Cross-client schema change: Telegram / TUI / any stored gate `input_schema` that already compiled the old pattern needs a compatibility story.

## Repro

1. Compile a `GateInputField` with `type=word` (or inspect `_TYPE_SCHEMA_FRAGMENTS[InputType.WORD]["pattern"]`).
2. Validate `"owner/repo"` against that JSON Schema fragment: it matches `^\S+(?![\s\S])`.
3. Call `InputArg(name="x", type=InputType.WORD).validate_and_convert("owner/repo")`: it raises `MacroValidationError`.

## Impact

Gate forms and the typed macro/workflow binder disagree on the same `word`/`agent` value. Clients can submit values the schema accepts and the command then rejects; stored compiled schemas stay on the pre-hardening charset until recompiled.
